title: GS-TG: 3D Gaussian Splatting Accelerator with Tile Grouping for Reducing Redundant Sorting while Preserving Rasterization Efficiency
problem: 3D Gaussian Splatting rendering faces a fundamental trade-off: large tile sizes reduce redundant sorting but increase unnecessary rasterization computations, limiting real-time performance in novel view synthesis.
motivation: 3D Gaussian Splatting is faster than NeRF with high image quality, but cannot meet real-time FPS demands due to inefficient sorting-rasterization interaction across tile boundaries.
method: GS-TG groups small rectangular image tiles together during sorting—the phase that arranges which pixels to compute—to reduce redundant work, then uses binary flags during rendering (converting the scene to pixels) to identify which tiles actually need processing. This hybrid approach combines the efficiency of handling large regions together during sorting with the efficiency of computing only necessary regions during rendering, without requiring model retraining.
key_novelty: GS-TG is the first to address the sorting-rendering trade-off in 3D Gaussian Splatting through tile grouping and binary-flag identification, achieving 1.54x speedup without retraining.
contributions: Tile grouping strategy during sorting to reduce redundant operations across small tiles.
Bitmask-based rasterization enabling efficient sharing of sorting results across tile groups.
Lossless acceleration achieving 1.54x speedup over SOTA 3D-GS accelerators, compatible with prior optimization techniques.
primary_theme: 3D Gaussian Splatting acceleration via tile grouping
